evals.prompt: We live in herdr worktrees and every new one needs the same two chores: copy .env across from the main checkout, then run npm install. Can you write me a herdr plugin that just does this whenever a worktree gets created? Node is fine, everyone here has it. Also the whole team shares this, so make it something I can put on GitHub later.
evals.expected_output: A plugin directory with a valid herdr-plugin.toml declaring an [[events]] hook on the exact event name worktree.created, plus a Node command that filters early, exits 0 when not applicable, calls herdr through HERDR_BIN_PATH, and keeps durable state out of the plugin root.
expectations: A herdr-plugin.toml exists declaring all four required top-level fields: id, name, version, and min_herdr_version
The manifest declares a top-level platforms list
The manifest declares an [[events]] entry whose on value is exactly the string 'worktree.created' — 'worktree.create', 'worktree_created', or any other spelling fails this assertion
Running `herdr plugin link <plugin-dir>` returns a result object whose plugin has no 'warnings' key (unlink afterwards to leave the registry clean)

Every command value is an argv array of separate arguments — no element contains a space-separated command line like 'node index.js', and no element contains shell metacharacters (&&, |, >, $VAR, *) unless the array's first element is a shell such as bash/sh with -c
The event command invokes herdr via the HERDR_BIN_PATH environment variable with a fallback, not a bare hardcoded 'herdr'
The command reads the event payload from HERDR_PLUGIN_EVENT_JSON or HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON rather than assuming the worktree path from cwd alone
The command guards its work and exits with status 0 when the hook does not apply (for example when no .env exists in the source checkout) rather than throwing or exiting non-zero

No durable state, credential, log, or database file is written under HERDR_PLUGIN_ROOT or the plugin's own directory; anything durable goes to HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR and any user config to HERDR_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR
The response does not claim the plugin needs registration, an SDK, an import of a herdr library, or any runtime action-registration call
No README.md-only deliverable: the actual manifest and the actual Node command file are both written to disk

evals.prompt: My herdr plugin is broken and I'm losing my mind. It's supposed to log a line every time a worktree gets created. `herdr plugin link` works fine — no errors, exit 0, it shows up in `herdr plugin list`. But nothing ever happens when I make a worktree. The plugin is at evals/files/broken-worktree-notify/. Can you figure out what's wrong and fix it?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis identifying the misspelled event name as the reason the hook never fires, an explanation that link reports this only through a warnings field rather than an error, and fixes for the single-string argv command and the state file written into the plugin root.
expectations: Identifies the misspelled event name (on = 'worktree.create') as the root cause of the hook never firing, and states the correct name is 'worktree.created'
Explains that herdr does not reject an unknown event name — the link succeeds and the only evidence is a 'warnings' entry in the response, e.g. "unknown event 'worktree.create'"
Names a concrete way to surface that warning, such as re-running `herdr plugin link` and reading the warnings field, or `herdr plugin list --json`
Identifies that command = ["bash notify.sh"] is a single argv element and therefore makes herdr look for a binary literally named 'bash notify.sh'; the fix splits it into ["bash", "notify.sh"]
Explains that herdr never runs commands through a shell, so the single string is not word-split the way a shell would split it

Identifies that notify.sh writes its log to $HERDR_PLUGIN_ROOT/seen-worktrees.log and that the plugin root is a managed checkout replaced on reinstall, so durable state belongs in HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR
The fixed notify.sh writes its log under HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR
The corrected manifest links with no warnings key: `herdr plugin link <dir>` returns a plugin object without 'warnings' (unlink afterwards)
Mentions `herdr plugin log list` as where a failing command's stderr, spawn error, or exit code actually surfaces, since plugin stdout is captured rather than printed
Does not attribute the failure to the plugin being disabled, to a missing herdr restart, to a permissions problem, or to any cause other than the three real defects
The diagnosis is grounded in the actual file contents rather than generic plugin-debugging advice that would apply to any plugin

evals.prompt: In herdr, when I click a Jira ticket URL in a terminal pane it opens my browser, which I hate. Our tickets look like https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/APP-5329. I'd rather it pop the ticket open in a split pane next to me using the `jira` CLI I already have installed. Bash please, I don't want a node dependency for this. macOS.
evals.expected_output: A plugin with a [[link_handlers]] entry whose regex matches the Jira URL and whose action names an action declared in the same plugin, an action that reads the clicked URL from the environment and opens a [[panes]] entrypoint with split placement via HERDR_BIN_PATH.
expectations: The manifest declares a [[link_handlers]] entry with a pattern and an action field

The link handler's pattern is a regex that matches https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/APP-5329 and does not match an arbitrary unrelated URL such as https://github.com/foo/bar/issues/1 (verify by testing the regex against both strings)
The link handler's action value names an action id declared by the same plugin — not a pane id, and not an id belonging to no entrypoint
The manifest declares a [[panes]] entrypoint, and the pane opens with split placement (either placement = 'split' in the manifest or --placement split on the open command)
The action command reads the clicked URL from HERDR_PLUGIN_CLICKED_URL, or parses clicked_url out of HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON
The action opens the pane by calling `herdr plugin pane open` through HERDR_BIN_PATH, passing the URL or ticket key to the pane via --env, rather than trying to render the ticket itself
Running `herdr plugin link <plugin-dir>` returns a result whose plugin has no 'warnings' key (unlink afterwards)
Every command is an argv array of separate elements, with any shell pipeline confined inside a bash -c argument
If the response describes the click gesture to the user, it says Control+click and does not tell a macOS user to use Command+click
The action exits 0 without erroring when no clicked URL is present in the environment
Does not claim herdr can open the URL in a browser-like or non-terminal plugin UI, and does not invent a manifest field for browser interception

evals.prompt: I want to write my next herdr plugin in Rust for once — just an action that tells me whether the current workspace's git checkout is dirty. I'm on macOS and Linux, no Windows. The thing I can't figure out: if someone installs this from GitHub, how does the binary actually get built? Set it up for me.
evals.expected_output: A Rust plugin with a [[build]] entry running cargo, an action whose command points at the compiled binary by a path relative to the plugin root, and an explanation that build runs on install but never on link so local authors must build the working tree themselves.
expectations: The manifest declares a [[build]] entry whose command runs cargo to build the binary (e.g. ['cargo', 'build', '--release'])

The action's command points at the compiled binary via a path relative to the plugin directory (e.g. './target/release/<name>'), and the response explains this resolves because runtime commands run with the plugin directory as their working directory
States explicitly that [[build]] commands run during `herdr plugin install` but NOT during `herdr plugin link`, so a locally linked plugin must be built by hand first
The manifest declares platforms as exactly linux and macos, without windows
A Cargo.toml and a src/main.rs are both written to disk, and `cargo build` in the plugin directory completes with exit code 0
`cargo build` produces no compiler warnings (verify the build output is clean, not merely successful)
The Rust code reads HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON and uses a workspace path from it (such as workspace_cwd) to decide which checkout to inspect, rather than relying only on the process cwd
Context fields deserialized from HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON are treated as optional/absent-tolerant rather than unwrapped as guaranteed present
The response states that the user's machine must already have cargo, and that herdr reports a failed build without installing any toolchain
Explains that a failing [[build]] aborts `herdr plugin install` and the plugin is never registered
Does not suggest committing the compiled binary to the repository as the way to make install work

evals.prompt: Right, my herdr plugin works on my machine — linked locally and doing its job. Now I want other people to be able to actually get it, and ideally have it show up in the herdr marketplace thing. What do I actually have to do?
evals.expected_output: Publishing guidance covering the GitHub topic herdr-plugin as the entire marketplace mechanism, the install shorthand, min_herdr_version discipline, and the install-versus-link differences, without inventing a submission or review process.
expectations: States that marketplace listing requires adding the GitHub topic 'herdr-plugin' to a public repository containing a herdr-plugin.toml
Does NOT invent a submission form, registry account, publish command, review or approval process, or any marketplace step beyond the GitHub topic — inventing any of these fails this assertion

Gives the install command in the correct GitHub shorthand form, `herdr plugin install owner/repo` (optionally with /subdir), and does not present a URL, a git clone, or a local path as the way others install it
Explains that min_herdr_version should be the oldest herdr version supporting the features the plugin actually uses, not the version on the author's machine
Mentions that the marketplace index is automatic and refreshes periodically (roughly every 30 minutes) rather than appearing instantly on demand
Notes that [[build]] commands run on install (unlike link), so a plugin needing a build step must have that declared before others install it
Advises documenting required toolchains (cargo, npm, bun, lua, etc.) since herdr reports build failures but never installs toolchains
Mentions that there is no `herdr plugin update` — refreshing a GitHub-managed plugin means reinstalling
Points at `herdr plugin config-dir <id>` as what setup instructions should tell users to run, rather than hardcoding a config path
Advises that credentials belong in HERDR_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR and must not be committed to the repo or written into the plugin root
Mentions that install shows users a preview of the source and commands, and that herdr does not sandbox or review plugin code, so readable manifests and scripts matter
